# PubMed novelty fixture recovery screen, 25 September 2026

The [protocol](novelty-fixture-recovery-prereg-v1.json) was committed as `e313bdd2` before this screen. The [runner](novelty_fixture_recovery.py) sent the three frozen identifier-first queries through the current `pubmed_fulltext` parameter mapper and maintained loopback MCP client. It used an empty isolated cache, ephemeral loopback shared secret, no ambient provider or retrieval credentials, and no model inference. Exactly three outer PubMed tool calls completed without a reported error; no raw server logs or full abstracts were added to the repository. The unmodified [result](novelty-fixture-recovery-results-v1.json) has SHA-256 `8f00b038a38295034086dfeb7c65c0c618669144839d674a184d3afb28483e15`. Each result carries its exact wire query, returned IDs/titles, abstract hash, and bounded selected-rung record.

The predeclared exact target-PMID recall remains **0/3**, equal to the earlier raw-prose screen. Each PubMed abstract below was inspected in the isolated cache against the frozen draft; the labels address that draft's *central mechanism*, not general topical similarity.

| Draft | Chosen search rung | Returned PMID and abstract-level judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TDP-43 / STMN2 cryptic polyadenylation and axonal repair | 2, anchored on TDP-43 and STMN2; nine search IDs | [42359165](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42359165/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: an ALS treatment review names STMN2 downstream of TDP-43 but does not establish the draft's cryptic polyadenylation/axonal-repair link. [42596024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42596024/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: tests UNC13A cryptic splicing in Alzheimer's disease and explicitly says STMN2 did not show the same cognitive association. [42619804](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42619804/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: detects STMN2 cryptic transcripts in C9ORF72 FTD synaptic material, without the motor-neuron axonal-repair mechanism. |
| SARS-CoV-2 ACE2 / TMPRSS2 airway entry | 2, anchored on TMPRSS2 and ACE2-dependent; nine search IDs | [42354881](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42354881/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: a post-COVID cardiovascular review mentions ACE2 and limited cardiac TMPRSS2, not reduced TMPRSS2 in airway infection. [40166473](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40166473/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: an ACE2-dependent spike-pseudovirus drug screen lacks a TMPRSS2 reduction test. [39536058](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39536058/) — **related_without_mechanism_support**: compares ACE2-independent sarbecovirus entry supported by TMPRSS2-related proteases, a different mechanism and virus context. |
| Tumor Qa-1b / NKG2A inhibition | 3, unanchored OR; nine search IDs | [42666366](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42666366/) — **unrelated**: brain vascular malformation language mapping. [42775084](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42775084/) — **unrelated**: fungal metabolite biosynthesis. [42740829](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42740829/) — **unrelated**: antibiotic biosynthesis. None addresses the tumor immune mechanism. |

The first two searches became more topically focused than their raw-prose counterparts, but their known target papers are absent from the first three and none of these abstracts establishes its full positive mechanism. The third search fell through to the broad OR rung and returned wholly unrelated papers. This screen does **not** qualify any of the three positive fixtures, prove novelty, or justify releasing the query rewrite as a scientific-quality improvement. It does show where the maintained retrieval path relaxed each query; publication-date ordering and fulltext preference are still code-supported possible contributors, not isolated causal findings. The original and recovery screens were separated in time, so their topical difference is descriptive rather than a controlled paired quality estimate.

No new retrieval trial will be run in this cycle. The next bounded investigation should diagnose why older known prior art is absent from the nine IDs of the two anchored searches and why the Qa-1b query cannot satisfy its subject anchors, then preregister a **matched** candidate/baseline test with distinct-idea controls before another quality claim.
